waypoints.label: Trailhead
waypoints.title: Start at the Granite Creek trailhead
waypoints.caption: Gravel lot at the end of FR 4410 with a vault toilet and a map kiosk. The trail leaves from the north end, past the gate.

waypoints.label: Ranger station
waypoints.title: Check in at the Granite Creek guard station
waypoints.caption: Small log guard station 200 yards up the trail. Fill out the free wilderness permit at the box on the porch.

waypoints.label: Loop junction
waypoints.title: Bear left at the loop junction
waypoints.caption: Signed four-way junction under big hemlocks. Take the left fork toward First Pass so the steep climb is on fresh legs; you'll come back down the right fork.

waypoints.label: Granite Creek ford
waypoints.title: Ford Granite Creek
waypoints.caption: Knee-deep in June, ankle-deep by August. A log jam 30 yards upstream is drier when the water is low.

waypoints.label: Miners' cabin
waypoints.title: Pass the old miners' cabin
waypoints.caption: A collapsed 1920s cabin on the right, with a rusted stove still inside. Don't climb on it; the roof beams are loose.

waypoints.label: Switchbacks
waypoints.title: Settle in for 34 switchbacks
waypoints.caption: The climb to First Pass starts here: 1,400 ft in 1.8 mi on a well-graded tread. Most people take 75–90 minutes. There's shade until the last ten turns.

waypoints.label: Cedar Range view
waypoints.title: Look back at the Cedar Range
waypoints.caption: A rock bench on the outside of switchback 22 with a view west over the whole Cedar Range.

waypoints.label: Upper Basin trail
waypoints.title: Upper Basin trail: last easy way down
waypoints.caption: Unsigned trail dropping right (east) to the Upper Basin road, 2.1 mi of steady downhill. If you're behind schedule or the sky looks bad, turn back here: past First Pass there's no shortcut for 5 miles.

waypoints.label: First Pass
waypoints.title: Cross First Pass and stay left
waypoints.caption: Broad rocky notch with a cairn. A climbers' path goes straight up the ridge; stay left on the main trail, which drops slightly toward Tarn Lake.

waypoints.label: Tarn Lake
waypoints.title: Tarn Lake
waypoints.caption: Small, cold lake in a granite bowl. The outlet stream on the south shore is the best place to filter. Camping only at the posted sites.

waypoints.label: Scree traverse
waypoints.title: Cross the scree field slowly
waypoints.caption: About 300 yards of loose talus with a faint path marked by cairns. Test each step; rocks shift. Poles help. Late in the day, rockfall from the cliff above is more common.

waypoints.label: Granite Saddle
waypoints.title: Top out on Granite Saddle
waypoints.caption: The high point at 7,240 ft: wide granite slabs, big views both ways, and wind. Lunch spot, but bring a layer.

waypoints.label: Saddle junction
waypoints.title: Turn right onto the Ridge Return trail
waypoints.caption: Signed junction just past the saddle. Straight on goes to Crater Lakes (6 mi, no return loop). Turn right and start down.

waypoints.label: North snowfield
waypoints.title: Expect snow on the north slope
waypoints.caption: This shaded slope holds snow into mid-July. Early season, it's a firm, steep traverse: microspikes and an early start (before it softens) make it much safer.

waypoints.label: Hidden Meadow spring
waypoints.title: Hidden Meadow spring
waypoints.caption: A spring piped through a wooden trough at the top of the meadow.

waypoints.label: Fire road
waypoints.title: Fire road crossing
waypoints.caption: An old fire road crosses the trail here. Turning right follows it 3.2 mi down to the trailhead road: longer than the trail, but gentler on sore knees and easy to follow in the dark.

waypoints.label: Lookout ruins
waypoints.title: Pass the lookout ruins
waypoints.caption: Concrete footings from a 1930s fire lookout on a knoll left of the trail. A 2-minute side trip gives the last big view of the day.

waypoints.label: Return junction
waypoints.title: Back at the loop junction: turn left for the trailhead
waypoints.caption: You're back at the four-way junction from the morning, coming in from the east. Turn left (south) and retrace the 0.9 mi stem to the car.
